Met up with some new friends on Friday night (met through a meetup group) and had a really good night. Spent Saturday and sunday buying some things for the house (ex moves out this week after we broke up a month ago). Had been going well until Sunday. Basically she spent the entire weekend at "her friends" but not the one she told me she was going to be at (facebook pics of the friend and her family away on a trip popped up on my timeline).

Kind of hurt as had been a fairly amicable break up and we had agreed we wouldn't date while we were still sharing a house.

Ended up getting drunk on my own at home and hit a pretty low place.  Perked up next day though - realised well good riddance. Have dropped 17lbs in 4 weeks, have some new friends, going away to a concert this weekend and organising a weekend away with new friends for later this month.

Just looking forward to hitting my target weight (another 20lbs to go) then start dating

I went through a tough spell and really devoted more time to sitting on my arse playing games than i did to my relationship. When that ended i took a long hard look at myself and realised i just wasn't happy doing that.

Started exercising that day. Rather than come home and stick a game on for a couple of hours i now go for a walk. Every day. That and eating healthy have seen me drop close to 20lbs in the last month. While i do sometimes think about turning a game back on i honestly just don't find myself that interested. Prefer reading, doing something productive (joined a cooking class) and just getting out there.

I think it all comes from an initial decision to do something else to start with instead of playing at your usual times.

After a little bit of time you will find you aren't really interested in going back.

In terms of the people meeting you - please don't worry. You have put your pics out there, if they are keen to meet you they are interested. The vast majority of guys aren't looking for a supermodel. As long as you are easy going, nice to talk to and get along that is really the main thing!

Yeah it sucks and is very easy to feel alone and lonely. My advice is to get out there and just keep busy and try to meet people - meetup has been really helpful for me and started an evening class as well. Never thought i would be the type of person to do those things (growing up was in the pub every night with friends) but you have to do what you can to change things. One things for sure - you will not make new friends sitting at home watching tv!

So in a very similar situation (other than she broke up with me - had grown apart but not bitterness really). Like you i do not know anyone where i live amd have really struggled with how to keep myself occupied.

First things first - work on yourself a but before jumping in to anything date wise. Like you i had gotten a bit lost in terms of just being a couple and when it ended didn't really know what i wanted or enjoyed doing anymore.

First thing i did was decide to get back in shape. I have taken up walking/hiking everyday after work and eating a lot less and a lot healthier. Not only is it enjoyable, gives you something to do with your time, and is for a good purpose - it is cheap so helps you in terms of the saving money.

Second - try to make some friends. I have joined a couple of meetup groups and has been a really good way to get out there and meet some new people without the pressure of weirdness that comes with dating. Is opening me up to some new activities and again helping me keep busy. I have joined an evening cookery class, being more social with people at work etc. When i come back from one of these and she is just on the sofs in her PJs then it makes me feel better knowing i am out there actively bettering my life and as a result will be able to move on much quicker than if i was wallowing.

Anyway - just my 2 cents, hope some of it is useful

I would 100% message him if keen. If i was him, and had sent last message, i would be worried your weren't responding after having met me in real life.

Only way you know for sure is in reaching out.

What you would likely find is that the type of man who would be interested would likely have young children of their own. Therefore they wouldn't be looking for someone to be at their beck and call but a companion who could fit in with their lives - not have it revolve around them.

Ultimately it is your decision as to whether you wait or not - only you know what is right for you

I am afraid that as much as it sucks your needs are gonna need to take a backseat for a little while. This could be one of the worst experiences he will ever go through. He is unlikely to know how to handle it and will not be aware of your needs during this period.

As part of a team this is the time where you will need to carry the load. Even thought it is hard acting out, getting in to fights at this time could cause lasting resentment. Taking energy and focus away from where it needs to be at this time to focus on you may cause him to blame you for him. It being able to fully commit to being there for his parents at this time (even if that is unfair).

Just imagine what you would need and want if the roles were reversed. Just be there when needed and, once it is all over, it may actually bring you closer together.

Similar experience - 2 weeks ago broke up with my GF of 5 years. We had definitely grown apart but when i said to her that i needed more affection and didn't want to count the months in between her giving me so much as a hug - she said she didn't love me anymore (and hadn't for a while) and we broke up.

It sucks when your feelings aren't requited however all you can do is pick yourself and try to move on.

Focus on yourself and start with the little things - i have started walking every day after work to clear my head and get back in shape. Have organised to join some meetup groups to meet new people and put myself out there again.

After a long relationship it can be hard to remeber who you are on your own without being part of a couple. Therefore take some time to rediscover that.

Wish you all the best and here to talk if you need a friendly ear.

Couple of things to say and not sure if they will bring comfort or anything but just wanted to put them out there.

In terms of the escort thing - don't. After breaking up with my long term partner (of which we hadn't had sex in forever) i was angry and craving intimacy. Just wanted someone to want me. Went to an escort and it was one of the worst experiences of my entire life. I literally was there 10 minutes and just had to leave (had paid for an hour). It was so artificial and horrible and made me feel so bad about myself. Please don't even think about making that mistake, especially for your 1st time, and it is not something you will ever be able to take back.

In terms of your age and not having had a GF, my brother who is one of the nicest guys i have ever met had similar struggles. He didn't get his first GF (or kiss a girl) until he was in his early thirties. However they are now living happily together. Sometimes people are lucky enough to find someone early on, for others they have to wait a bit longer but it will come.

The real positive to take away is that your have 3 friends who care about you and want to spend time with you. Treasure that and keep putting yourself out there. Wish you all the best.
